title: Clopen pullback detects bijectivity and openness between profinite spaces
statement: Use the universe conventions of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P,Q$ be compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological spaces, where compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover, Hausdorff means that distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods, and totally disconnected means that every connected subset has at most one point. Let $h:P\to Q$ be continuous. Write $\operatorname{Clop}(Z)$ for the open and closed subsets of a space $Z$. Suppose that $h^{-1}:\operatorname{Clop}(Q)\to\operatorname{Clop}(P)$ is bijective. Then $h$ is injective and surjective. For every clopen $U\subseteq P$, its image $h(U)$ is the unique clopen $V\subseteq Q$ with $h^{-1}(V)=U$. Moreover $h$ is open: $h(O)$ is open in $Q$ for every open subset $O\subseteq P$. Empty spaces are allowed.

source.place: Agent separation and finite-subcover consequence of Tag 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), using its pointwise clopen-basis consequence. This statement is not the finite-refinement assertion of the tag.

proof.text: For distinct x,y in P, the complement of the closed singleton {y} is an open neighbourhood of x. The pointwise clopen basis [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis] gives a clopen U containing x and excluding y. Surjectivity of clopen pullback writes U as the inverse image of a target clopen V. Equal images of x and y would then imply y belongs to U, a contradiction. Hence h is injective.

source.place: Agent argument using the pointwise clopen-basis consequence of Tag 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), carried by lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis.

proof.text: The image h(P) is closed, because a continuous map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is closed (Mathlib Continuous.isClosedMap). If q is missing from the image, its complement is an open neighbourhood of q. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis] to obtain a clopen V containing q and contained in that complement. Its inverse image is empty, hence equals the inverse image of the empty clopen. Injectivity of clopen pullback forces V to be empty, contradicting q in V. This proves surjectivity, including when P is empty.

source.place: Agent shorter closed-image version of the original finite-subcover argument, using Mathlib Continuous.isClosedMap and the pointwise clopen-basis consequence of Tag 08ZZ.

proof.text: For a source clopen U, surjectivity of clopen pullback gives a target clopen V with inverse image U. Since h is surjective, the image of that inverse image is V, so h(U)=V is clopen and its inverse image is U. For any other target clopen W with inverse image U, the same image-of-preimage identity gives W=h(U). This proves all three clopen-image clauses.

source.place: Agent set-theoretic identification of the image using the bijectivity established in steps 1 and 2.

proof.text: Apply the clopen-basis criterion for an open map (Mathlib IsTopologicalBasis.isOpenMap_iff) to [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis]. Every basis clopen has open image by step 3. The criterion takes unions of basis elements and commutes their images with unions, including the empty union, so h is open.

Step 1 (injectivity): Hausdorffness and a clopen basis set U with x∈U⊆A exclude x', and V with h^{-1}V=U separates h(x) from h(x'). Step 2 (surjectivity): if q∉h(P), clopens excluding q cover h(P); compactness gives finitely many, and their union W has h^{-1}W=h^{-1}Q, so W=Q by injectivity, a contradiction (the empty subcover is handled). Step 3: h(U)=V by step 2, and V is unique by injectivity. Step 4: O is a union of clopens, so h(O) is open. All steps are genuinely elementary. Small cases checked: empty P and/or Q, constant map 2→1 (not surjective on clopens), inclusion 1→2 (not injective on clopens), finite discrete spaces.
